adversarial_checks: Corrected the prior 24/25 May release date rather than silently overwriting it.
The May 14 Assembly action and May 19 physical release are encoded separately; a five-day gap requires custody records.
FRUS says the Assembly acted under Constitution Article 49, but the Korean resolution and constitutional text must still be opened before treating the US footnote as the sole legal interpretation.
The May 19 release does not prove May 25 martial law was declared solely to re-arrest So Min-ho.
The May 25 re-arrest being the first martial-law act in US reporting does not by itself identify the Korean official who authored the arrest order.
Investigator identity resolution uses constituency/party context to prevent modern-name conflation, but Hanja/life dates remain open where not independently verified.
Committee membership does not imply each investigator agreed with every finding in Report No.1; signatures/minority views must be checked in the original.
Kim Jeong-gi's repeated investigative roles establish institutional centrality, not neutrality or correctness.
So Min-ho's prior oversight activity and conflict with Rhee establish political context but do not determine the shooting-case merits.
The prosecution's 'nonpolitical' characterization and the government's political conflict with So can coexist as competing contemporaneous frames; neither is silently privileged.

history_debt_updates.update: So Min-ho custody sequence narrowed to Assembly release action 1952-05-14 -> physical release 1952-05-19 -> martial-law re-arrest 1952-05-25. The individual re-arrest order author and presidential command link remain unresolved.
